newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian BTC sees 96 net, dividend down.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian BTC sees 96 net, dividend down.

text.p: Slovenian shopping centre and warehouse operator BTC said on Tuesday its 1996 net profit fell to around 506.3 million tolars ($3.3 million) from 730 million the previous year.
It also announced it would slash its dividend to 400 tolars from 900, the company added.
Speaking at a news conference, Joze Mermal, head of BTC's management board, traced the decline in net profit to interest payments on a recent bond issue.
The company in October 1996 issued 12-year bonds to the value of $20 million with a nominal value of 100 marks ($59) and a fixed annual interest rate of 10.5 percent.

He said investment in 1997 would decrease to $3.5 million from $5.3 million in 1996, but the company expects its turnover to rise by eight to 10 percent annually over the next five years due to new investments in previous years.
In 1996 the company's turnover rose to 4.4 billion tolars from 3.7 billion.
"In 1996 alone, we opened 10,000 square metres (107,640 square feet) of new shopping areas," Mermal said.
He said in the next few years the firm planned to modernise its facilities, build a new business centre in Ljubljana and invest in new parking areas around its shopping centres.
BTC manages shopping and warehousing centres in the capital, in the south in Novo Mesto and in the eastern cities of Murska Sobota and Ptuj.
On Tuesday BTC's shares, which are listed on the main market of the Ljubljana bourse, led the day's decliners, down 9.82 percent to 13,230 tolars on volume of 713 shares.

"The drop is mainly a result of a techical correction and does not indicate a longer downward trend as BTC has so far realised most of its plans and is seen as a good long-term investment," one broker said. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
